title: Targeted immune drugs: JAK inhibitors, IL-6, IL-17 and co-stimulation blockers
ariaLabel: Schematic of targeted immune drugs: cytokines signal through JAK kinases inside the cell, interleukin-6 acts on its receptor, interleukin-17 and 23 drive skin and joint inflammation, and T cells need a second co-stimulation signal. JAK inhibitors block the kinases, tocilizumab blocks the IL-6 receptor, secukinumab and ustekinumab block IL-17 or IL-23, and abatacept blocks co-stimulation.
caption: Schematic, not to scale. Flow and levels are qualitative and illustrative; no dose, concentration or lipid value is shown or implied.
blockInfo: A drug of the chosen class acting at this step (generic teaching symbol, not a named drug's shape). Less passes here, with the effects shown at the cholesterol and the LDL receptors.

nodes.label: Cytokine signal
nodes.info: Many cytokines signal through JAK kinases and STAT proteins.

nodes.label: STAT signalling
nodes.info: Signals that switch on inflammatory genes.

nodes.label: Interleukin-6
nodes.info: Interleukin-6 drives fever, acute phase proteins and joint inflammation.

nodes.label: IL-17 and IL-23
nodes.info: Cytokines of the Th17 pathway that drive psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis and spondyloarthritis.

nodes.label: Th17 effect
nodes.info: Skin and joint inflammation through the Th17 pathway.

nodes.label: T cell second signal
nodes.info: T cells need a second signal (CD28 with CD80 or CD86) to be fully activated.

nodes.label: Autoimmune inflammation
nodes.info: A teaching score for inflammation in an autoimmune disease.

edges.label: JAK-STAT
edges.info: JAK inhibitors (tofacitinib, baricitinib, upadacitinib) are small oral molecules that block JAK kinases and so many cytokine signals at once. They raise the risk of infection (including shingles), clots and some cancers.

edges.label: IL-6 receptor
edges.info: Tocilizumab and sarilumab block the IL-6 receptor. They can hide fever and a raised CRP when infection is present.

edges.label: IL-17 or IL-23
edges.info: Secukinumab and ixekizumab block IL-17; ustekinumab blocks IL-12 and IL-23; guselkumab and risankizumab block IL-23.

edges.label: co-stimulation
edges.info: Abatacept is a CTLA-4 fusion protein that binds CD80 and CD86, so the second signal is not given and T cells are not fully activated.
More T cell activation raises inflammation.

sources: Where each class acts. JAK inhibitors block cytokine signalling inside the cell, tocilizumab blocks the IL-6 receptor, secukinumab and ustekinumab block IL-17 or IL-23, and abatacept blocks T cell co-stimulation. This is standard teaching in the pharmacology texts the PrepNucleus lessons cite (Katzung; KD Tripathi) and were not checked against a linked source here, so they are flagged for review.
simplified: Anti-TNF and other drugs (own figure), anti-CD20 and anti-IL-1 and IL-5 drugs, which disease each drug is used for, infection screening, clot and cancer warnings for JAK inhibitors, monitoring and cost are left out. Inflammation is drawn as a teaching score. Levels and the size of each effect are illustrative. The drug choices are teaching toggles of a class: no named drug, dose or schedule is shown or implied, and the figure does not say who should or should not take any of them.
